Rashi on Niddah 27a:10:1.hebrew: לבית החיצון - לבית אחר, שהבית טהור:
Rashi on Niddah 27a:10:1.english: To the outer room - To another room, [meaning] that the room is pure.

Rashi on Niddah 27a:11:1.hebrew: אמרו לו למה - מאי שנא בית ראשון דמטמית ליה? אמר להו: לפי שאינו, הואיל וטלטלוהו נמוק:
Rashi on Niddah 27a:11:1.english: They said to him: Why - How is the first house different, that you declare it impure? He said to them: "Because it does not exist" — since they moved it, it disintegrated.

Rashi on Niddah 27a:12:1.hebrew: מ"ט דר"ש - נהי דנמוק, מ"מ כל גופו של מת כאן הוה, וה"ל כרקב וכנצל [בשר המת שנימוח ונעשה ליחה סרוחה]:
Rashi on Niddah 27a:12:1.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon - Granted that [the fetus] dissolved, nevertheless the entire body of the corpse was here, and it should be like corpse dust and like corpse broth [the flesh of a corpse that dissolved and became a foul liquid].

Rashi on Niddah 27a:12:2.hebrew: ממין אחר - אפי' ממין טומאה, אם אינה שוה לה, בטלה:
Rashi on Niddah 27a:12:2.english: Of another type - Even [if it is] of a type of ritual impurity, if it is not equivalent to it, it is nullified.

Rashi on Niddah 27a:13:1.hebrew: אחיכו עליה - אמרו ליה: פשיטא, מאי שנא טעמייהו מטעמיה? כולה חדא מילתא אמרי:
Rashi on Niddah 27a:13:1.english: They laughed at him - They said to him: [It is] obvious! How is their reason different from his reason? They are all saying the same thing!

Rashi on Niddah 27a:14:1.english: Even a matter like this - That leads to ridicule.

Rashi on Niddah 27a:14:2.english: A person should say - Perhaps through his words they will tell him the reason.

Rashi on Niddah 27a:14:3.english: And let him not be silent - And let him say, "I will explain [it] to him."

Rashi on Niddah 27a:14:4.hebrew: אם נבלת - עצמך על ד"ת, סופך להתנשא:
Rashi on Niddah 27a:14:4.english: If you have abased - Yourself over words of Torah, you will ultimately be exalted.

Rashi on Niddah 27a:14:5.hebrew: ואם זמות - ושתקת, סופך לשום יד על פה, שלא תדע להשיב לשואלין:
Rashi on Niddah 27a:14:5.english: And if you muzzled [yourself] - And you remained silent, your end will be to place a hand on [your] mouth, for you will not know how to answer those who ask.

Rashi on Niddah 27a:15:2.hebrew: רקב - רקבובית של מת, וזה שיעורו לטמא באהל, הלכה למשה מסיני:
Rashi on Niddah 27a:15:2.english: Rot - Decayed matter of a corpse, and this is its measure to defile in a tent, [which is] a halakha to Moses from Sinai.

Rashi on Niddah 27a:17:1.hebrew: א"א - אף על גב דרובא רקב, אי אפשר למקום שנפל העפר שלא תהא גרגר של רקב בין שני גרגרים של עפר, ובטל הרקב, ובציר לו שיעורא דתרוד:
Rashi on Niddah 27a:17:1.english: It is impossible - Even though the majority is corpse dust, it is impossible for the place where the earth fell not to have a grain of corpse dust between two grains of earth, and the corpse dust is nullified, and the measure of a ladleful is diminished.

Rashi on Niddah 27a:1:1.hebrew: חומר שני ולדות - אם זה זכר, חיישינן דלמא נקבה הוה ההוא דשליא, ותשב לזכר ולנקבה. ולרבנן דאמרי: המפלת חיה ועוף אינו ולד, מאי חומרא איכא בהאי ולד? מחמרינן עלה למימר: ליכא שום ולד ואין לה דם טוהר, והיינו חומרא דיליה. ומשום שליא מטמינן לה שבועים:
Rashi on Niddah 27a:1:1.english: The stringency of two offspring - If this [discharged fetus] is male, we are concerned that perhaps that [fetus] of the afterbirth was female, and she must observe [the stringencies of both] a male and a female. And according to the Rabbis, who say that [in the case of] a woman who discharges [the form of] a wild beast or a bird, it is not an offspring, what stringency is there regarding this offspring? We apply a stringency to her, to say that there is no offspring at all and she has no [days of] pure blood, and that is its stringency. And on account of the afterbirth, we deem her impure for two weeks.

Rashi on Niddah 27a:1:2.hebrew: שאני אומר - ולד הוה עם השליא, ונימוח שפיר של שליא:
Rashi on Niddah 27a:1:2.english: For I say - An offspring was with the afterbirth, and the gestational sac of the afterbirth disintegrated.

Rashi on Niddah 27a:1:3.english: A gestational sac - [This means] an offspring.

Rashi on Niddah 27a:1:4.hebrew: ושמא נימוחה שלייתו של שפיר - כלומר, ושלייתו של זה שלפנינו נימוח, וזו אינה שלו, הואיל ואינה קשורה בו. קתני מיהא: בזמן שקשורה עמהן:
Rashi on Niddah 27a:1:4.english: And perhaps the afterbirth of the fetus disintegrated - That is to say, the afterbirth of this [fetus] before us disintegrated, and this [afterbirth] is not its own, since it is not tied to it. At any rate, [the baraita] teaches: "When [the afterbirth] is tied to them."

Rashi on Niddah 27a:1:5.hebrew: תיובתא - דרבי, דאמר: דבר שאינו שאלת:
Rashi on Niddah 27a:1:5.english: A refutation - Of Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], who said: "You asked about a thing that does not exist."

Rashi on Niddah 27a:2:1.hebrew: אחר הולד - אבל יצתה שליא קודם, חוששין לאחר:
Rashi on Niddah 27a:2:1.english: After the offspring - But if an afterbirth emerged beforehand, we are concerned for another [offspring].

Rashi on Niddah 27a:5:1.english: This works out well according to the one who says, etc. - Their dispute is later in the chapter 'Benot Kutim' (Niddah 38b).

Rashi on Niddah 27a:5:2.hebrew: לסוף ז' - יום או יומים בתוך חדש ז' בסופו, דחיי:
Rashi on Niddah 27a:5:2.english: At the end of seven [months] - One or two days within the seventh month, at its end, for [the infant] is viable.

Rashi on Niddah 27a:5:3.hebrew: ואחד לתחלת תשעה - יום אחד בחדש, דהוו להו ל"ג:
Rashi on Niddah 27a:5:3.english: And one at the beginning of the ninth [month] - One day into the month, so that there are thirty-three [days].

Rashi on Niddah 27a:5:4.hebrew: אלא למ"ד אינה יולדת למקוטעים היכי משכחת לה - תרוייהו בחדש השביעי ליכא למימר, דחדש כולי האי לא הוי. ואם זה לסוף ז' וזה לסוף ט', טפי איכא. ואם זה בז' וזה בח', לא חיי; ומדקרי להו ולד ולא נפל, מכלל דבני קיימא נינהו:
Rashi on Niddah 27a:5:4.english: Rather, according to the one who says [that a woman] does not give birth in incomplete [months], how can you find [such a case]? - One cannot say [that] both of them [were born] in the seventh month, for a month is not that long. And if this one [was born] at the end of the seventh [month] and that one at the end of the ninth [month], there is more [time than that]. And if this one [was born] in the seventh [month] and that one in the eighth [month] — [the one born in the eighth month] does not live; and since [the text] calls them "offspring" and not "a miscarriage," it implies that they were viable.

Rashi on Niddah 27a:6:1.english: Reverse the teaching - [The teaching] of Rabbi Yoḥanan.

Rashi on Niddah 27a:6:2.hebrew: כ"ג לולד - משכחת לה דאחד נגמרה צורתו לתחלת ז' ואחד לסוף ז', דלכו"ע יולדת לז' יולדת למקוטעין:
Rashi on Niddah 27a:6:2.english: Twenty-three for an offspring - You can find [such a case] where the form of one was completed at the beginning of the seventh [month], and [that of] the other at the end of the seventh [month], as everyone agrees that a woman who gives birth at seven [months] can give birth to incomplete [months].

Rashi on Niddah 27a:8:1.hebrew: האמר מר כו' - קס"ד, בג' חדשים לא משכחת לה, אא"כ נתעברה זה אחר זה:
Rashi on Niddah 27a:8:1.english: Didn't the Master say, etc. - [The Gemara] presumed that with [a delay of] three months, you do not find it [possible] unless she conceived one after the other.

Tosafot on Niddah 27a:16:1.hebrew: מ"ט דר"ש - משום דבמתניתין אינו מזכיר כי אם ר"ש, קאמר מ"ט דר"ש. פ"ה: נהי דנימוק, מ"מ כל הגוף של המת כאן, וה"ל כרקב של מת וכנצל. וקשה, דא"כ מאי משני: "כל טומאה שנתערב בה מין אחר בטלה"? והיכי בעי למימר דבטל הולד משום דדם הלידה מבטל משהו מן הולד? כמו מלא תרוד דמייתי התם, ודאי דשיעורו מצומצם, כי יתבטל ממנו משהו בציר ליה שיעורא מן התרוד; אבל כי יתבטל מעט מן הולד, אכתי ישאר יותר מכזית או ממלא תרוד! לכך נראה לר"י, דנפל שבשליא אין עליו תורת נצל ורקב, כיון שאינו נגמר, ואינו בשר לטמא בכזית, אלא מטעם מת שלם. וה"פ: מ"ט דר"ש? הרי יש כאן מת שלם! ומשני: "כל טומאות שנתערבה כו'", ומהאי טעמא כי נתבטל ממנו משהו — טהור. והשתא מייתי שפיר ממלא תרוד רקב, ופריך: אדרבה כו', וה"נ השפיר מבטל משהו של מין אחר; ומשני רבי יוחנן: משום בטול ברוב נגעו בה, שדם הלידה והליחה רבה על כל השפיר, ומשבטל כולו בטל אף בבית ראשון. ור"ל סבר דאפילו בלא בטול ברוב טהור, משום בלבול צורה, שנטרף במימיו ונתבלבל צורתו לר"ש, אף בבית הראשון. ומדר"ל נמי יש להוכיח דלא מטמא משום רקב ונצל, דא"כ לא הוה מטהרינן משום בלבול; אלא ודאי טמא מטעם מת שלם, ובעי נמי ר"ל שלם בצורתו, ושאר אמוראי פליגי עליה בבלבול צורה, אך בעי שיהא שלם. וא"ת: למאי דס"ד דרבי שמעון מטהר אף בבית הפנימי משום בטול משהו, היכי קתני בברייתא "כשם שאינו בבית החיצון כך אינו בבית הפנימי" משום בטול משהו? הלא גם לרבי שמעון לא נתבטל כולו בבית הפנימי כמו בבית החיצון, אלא דמטהר משום בטול משהו! ויש לומר, דה"ק: כשם שאתה מודה בבית החיצון שנימוק, כך יש לטהר בבית הפנימי משום בטול משהו, דאין כאן מת שלם. ואם תאמר: בנזיר פרק כ"ג (דף נ.) דפריך: "על המת ועל כזית מן המת" — נזיר מגלח על כזית מן המת, מגלח על המת לא כ"ש? ומשני: "לא נצרכה אלא למת שאין בו כזית בשר ולא נתקשרו אבריו בגידין" — אמאי לא משני בשליא, שאינה מטמא אלא שלם? וי"ל, דשליא לא מקריא מת; א"נ, היינו הא דמשני התם:
Tosafot on Niddah 27a:16:1.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon? - Because in the mishna it does not mention anyone other than Rabbi Shimon, [Rav Pappa] says: "What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon?" Rashi explained: Granted that it disintegrated, nevertheless the entire body of the corpse is here, and it should be like the dust of a corpse (rekev) and like corpse decay (neṣel). And this is difficult: for if so, what is [the Gemara's] resolution, "Any impurity with which another kind was mixed is nullified"? And how can it wish to say that the offspring is nullified because the blood of childbirth nullifies a minute amount (mashehu) of the offspring? As in [the case of] the ladleful [of corpse dust] that it cites there (27a:15): certainly its measure is exact, [so] when a minute amount of it is nullified, its measure falls short of a ladleful; but when a small amount of the offspring is nullified, there will still remain more than an olive's bulk (kezayit) [for neṣel] or more than a ladleful [for rekev]! Therefore, it appears to the Ri that a miscarriage in an afterbirth is not subject to the law of neṣel or rekev, since it is not fully developed, and it is not [sufficiently developed] flesh to impart impurity with an olive's bulk; rather, [it can impart impurity only] by virtue of being a complete corpse (met shalem). And this is the explanation [of the Gemara]: "What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon?" — behold, is there not a complete corpse here? And it answers: "Any impurity with which [another kind] was mixed, etc." And for this reason, when a minute amount of it is nullified, it is pure [because it is no longer complete]. And now, [the Gemara] appropriately cites [the case of] a ladleful of corpse-dust (rekev), and challenges: "On the contrary, etc." — and so too here, [one could object: shouldn't] the gestational sac nullify a minute amount of the other kind? And Rabbi Yoḥanan answers: It was due to nullification by a majority (bittul be-rov) that they touched upon it [i.e., ruled it pure], for the blood of childbirth and the discharge outnumber the entire gestational sac; and once the whole of it is nullified, it is nullified even in the first room. And Reish Lakish holds that even without nullification by a majority it is pure, due to deformation of form (bilbul tzurah), as it was churned in its fluids and its form was deformed, according to Rabbi Shimon, even in the first room. And from Reish Lakish as well, there is proof that it does not impart impurity on account of rekev or neṣel, for if so, we would not have deemed it pure on account of deformation [of form]; rather, it is certainly impure [only] by virtue of being a complete corpse, and Reish Lakish furthermore requires that it be complete in its form; while the other Amora'im disagree with him regarding deformation of form, but [everyone] requires that it be complete. And if you say: According to what [the Gemara] initially thought, that Rabbi Shimon deems it pure even in the inner room on account of the nullification of a minute amount, how does the baraita teach: "Just as it does not exist in the outer room, so it does not exist in the inner room" on account of the nullification of a minute amount? Behold, even according to Rabbi Shimon, it was not completely nullified in the inner room as it was in the outer room, but rather he deems it pure on account of the nullification of a minute amount! And one can say that this is what it means: Just as you concede in the outer room that it disintegrated [and is pure because it is not a complete corpse], so too one should deem it pure in the inner room on account of the nullification of a minute amount, for there is no complete corpse here. And if you say: In Nazir, chapter Kohen Gadol (50a), where it challenges: "[A nazirite shaves] for a corpse, and for an olive's bulk from a corpse" — [if] a nazirite shaves for an olive's bulk from a corpse, is it not all the more so that he shaves for an [entire] corpse? And it answers: "It was necessary only for a corpse that does not contain an olive's bulk of flesh and its limbs were not bound with sinews" — why did it not answer with an afterbirth [containing a fetus], which imparts impurity only [when] complete? And one can say that an afterbirth is not called a corpse; alternatively, that is [in fact] what was answered there.

Tosafot on Niddah 27a:1:1.hebrew: חומר שני ולדות - פי' הקונטרס: לר"מ, דבחיה ועוף טמאה לידה, הוי חומר ב' ולדות — אם חיה ועוף הם זכר, יהבינן לה חומר שליא, דמספקינן בנקבה לטומאה, וחומר חיה ועוף לטהרה, דשמא אין ולד בשליא. וקשה לר"מ: אי חיה ועוף זכר, אמאי מספקא שליא בנקבה? הא הוי ספק ספיקא, דשמא אין בשליא ולד, ואפילו יש — שמא זכר הוא! ולכך י"ל: חומר ב' ולדות דקאמר, היינו לענין שהפילה שליא בשני אחר חיה ועוף. ולרבנן, דאמרי דאין טומאת לידה בחיה ועוף, לית לה ימי טוהר כלל, דשמא אין ולד בשליא, ומשום שליא נותנין לה חומרא דזכר ונקבה. וא"ת לרבנן: נימא שלא תשב רק ז' לטומאת לידה, דאימור אין ולד בשליא, ואפי' יש — שמא זכר הוא? וי"ל, דא"כ, אם תראה ביום ל"ד ותחזור ותראה ביום מ"א, איכא למימר נמי: אימור לא ילדה כלל, והויא במ"א שומרת יום כנגד יום, ואפי' איכא ולד — אימור נקבה היא, ושתי ראיות דם טוהר הוא. א"א בתרווייהו למיזל לקולא דסתרו אהדדי, אזלינן בתרווייהו לחומרא. וכן צ"ל אמתניתין דקתני: המפלת ואין ידוע אם ולד הוא, תשב לזכר ולנקבה ולנדה, אע"ג דאיכא ספק ספיקא: שמא לא ילדה, ואפי' ילדה — שמא זכר הוא, ואמאי תשב לנקבה? אלא ודאי כדפרישית:
Tosafot on Niddah 27a:1:1.english: The stringency of two offspring - Rashi explains that according to Rabbi Meir, who holds that [in the case of] an animal or a bird [a woman] is impure with the impurity of childbirth, "the stringency of two offspring" is: if the animal or bird is male, we assign to her the stringency of the afterbirth, as we treat it as a doubtful female regarding impurity, and the stringency of the animal or bird regarding purity, lest there be no offspring in the afterbirth. And this is difficult according to Rabbi Meir: If the animal or bird is male, why is the afterbirth treated as a doubtful female? Isn't there a double doubt (safek sefeika): perhaps there is no offspring in the afterbirth, and even if there is, perhaps it is male! And therefore, one must say: "The stringency of two offspring" which [the baraita] states is with regard to [a case where] she discharged the afterbirth on the second [day] after the animal or bird. And according to the Rabbis, who say that there is no impurity of childbirth for an animal or a bird, she has no days of purity at all, because perhaps there is no offspring in the afterbirth; and on account of the afterbirth, we impose upon her the stringency of a male and a female. And if you say: According to the Rabbis, let us say that she should sit only seven [days] for the impurity of childbirth, for say [perhaps] there is no offspring in the afterbirth, and even if there is, perhaps it is male? And one can say: For if so, if she sees [blood] on the thirty-fourth day and sees again on the forty-first day, one could also say: Say [perhaps] she did not give birth at all, and on the forty-first [day] she would be a woman who observes a day for a day (shomeret yom keneged yom); and even if there is an offspring, say it is female, and both sightings are blood of purity (dam tohar)! It is impossible to follow the leniency in both of them, because they contradict one another; [rather,] we follow the stringency in both of them. And so too one must say regarding our Mishnah, which teaches: "If a woman miscarries and it is not known whether it is an offspring, she must sit [observing the rules] for a male, for a female, and for a niddah" — even though there is a double doubt: perhaps she did not give birth, and even if she gave birth, perhaps it is male — why then should she sit for a female? Rather, it is certainly as I explained.

Tosafot on Niddah 27a:5:1.hebrew: אלא למ"ד אינה יולדת למקוטעין מאי איכא למימר - וא"ת: ונימא דנגמר צורתו ואשתהי עד שמיני, דהכי אית ליה לרבה תוספאה בפ' הערל (יבמות דף פ:), דעבד עובדא באשה שהלך בעלה למדינת הים וילדה לי"ב חדש, ואכשריה? ויש לומר, דרוב אמוראים לית להו דרבה תוספאה:
Tosafot on Niddah 27a:5:1.english: Rather, according to the one who says [that a woman] does not give birth in an incomplete [month], what is there to say - And if you say: Let us say that its form was completed [at seven months] and it was delayed until the eighth [month], for so Rabbah Tosfa'ah holds in the chapter [entitled] "HaArel" (Yevamot 80b), where he ruled in an incident involving a woman whose husband went overseas and she gave birth after twelve months, and he declared [the child] legitimate? And one can say that most Amora'im do not hold [in accordance with] Rabbah Tosfa'ah.
